lines: P-session-hardening (review-51 F4, review-56 note, review-63 notes): built, 4 commits on track/p-session-hardening (rebased onto main 623b377 on the coordinator's word), not pushed or landed. Land all four together: 526ee9a alone has the rule-4 defect ff0b682 fixes.

783384f fix(auth): nativeRefresh (native and admin_native) lower-cases rotationId once before derivation, rotateRefresh storage and the grace compare, as webRefresh does in 623b377. Before: last_rotation_id (uuid column, lower case) failed an upper-case retry inside the 30 s grace and revoked the family.

526ee9a fix(session): createRecoveryQueue moved to new api/session/recoveryQueue.ts and takes the scope. With navigator.locks the cookie refresh and the CSRF_INVALID recovery run under one exclusive lock per scope (boe.admin.session-recovery / boe.client.session-recovery), FIFO across and within tabs; without it the old in-tab queue, unchanged. sessionEnd.ts exports readStored.

ff0b682 fix(session): skip only on a confirmed fresh session. Flow in executeCookieRefresh: held user? -> getWebCsrf + holdsUser (finding-50/57, every path) -> if the stored CSRF token (localStorage boe.<scope>.csrfToken) changed since the tab queued, adoptAnotherTabsRotation reads the session with the access cookie alone (admin GET /v1/admin/session, client GET /v1/client/profile; existing read-only routes, unauthenticated: true): refused -> refresh as before; another user -> 'replaced' (ends revoked, no resend); same user -> adopt, 'rotated' (one resend). Temporary failures rethrow (session and holds kept).

2f251fb fix(session): review-63 N1 and N2. N1: the lock wait is bounded by DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS (20 s) via an AbortController passed as the request's signal, whose timer is cleared once the lock is granted, so only the wait can abort; the abort becomes TransportError('timeout'), so the read fails visibly, session and holds are kept, a write stays unknown (isUnknownWriteOutcome). A timer instead of AbortSignal.timeout: a slow granted step is never reported as a wait timeout, and fake timers can test it.

2f251fb N2: on adopt, the admin shell stores the principal from GET /v1/admin/session (roles, permissions), the client shell the principal from the CSRF read it just user-checked (the refresh path's shape, same scope.buildPrincipal on the server; the profile read has no accountStatus). Both after the user check, with the CSRF token, in one tokenStore.update.

Compatibility (rule 11): no route, contract, cookie, header, error code, token format or migration change. Released apps v0.14.7..v0.18.0 mint rotationId with crypto.randomUUID (lower case, no polyfill; git grep on each tag), so native tokens are byte-identical. Previous backend (CSRF read replaces the token): no revoke, one refresh (test). Web Locks needs a secure context; plain http and old WebViews keep today's behaviour.

Tests: backend authNative.integration 'an upper-case $channel rotationId replays within the grace and does not revoke the family', test.each over native and admin_native (admin routes registered in the same app, a support-role admin seeded).

Frontend src/shells/crossTabRefresh.test.ts, 14 cases (admin web, client web x 7), two runtimes sharing jsdom localStorage, a fake navigator.locks (FIFO, honours signal) and a stateful fake server: (1) both tabs read at once -> one refresh, no revoke, both hold the server's token and its current principal; (2) previous backend -> one refresh, no revoke; (3) the waiting tab's session read names another user -> ends revoked, no resend; (4) stored token changed, access not renewed -> probe 401 then refresh; (5) no navigator.locks -> single tab unchanged; (6) a tab waiting on a hung holder fails with the transport timeout at 20 s, sends nothing, keeps its session, outcome unknown; (7) a CSRF_INVALID recovery queued while another tab refreshes waits for the rotation, so no revoke and the write is resent with the token read after it.

Red controls (TESTED, runner, restored and cmp-identical, tree clean after). Runtime steps for the coordinator (UNVERIFIED; local stack on https or localhost so Web Locks exists):

R1 admin web: two tabs signed in as one admin. DevTools > Application > Cookies: delete boe_access (__Host-boe_access on https). Trigger a read in both tabs within a second. Expected: one tab GET /v1/auth/web/csrf, POST /v1/auth/web/refresh 200, its read; the other GET /v1/auth/web/csrf, GET /v1/admin/session 200, its read, no refresh. Both stay signed in; auth_sessions: active, revocation_reason null, generation +1.
R2 client web: same with boe_client_access; one POST /v1/auth/client/web/refresh, and GET /v1/client/profile in the other tab instead of a refresh.
R3 single tab: delete the access cookie, trigger a read: GET csrf, POST refresh, the read; no session or profile read. Unchanged.

R4 (optional, N1): with two tabs, stop the API mid-refresh (or throttle it to never answer); the waiting tab shows a timeout error after about 20 s instead of waiting for the first tab's retries, and stays signed in.

Doubtful or left: (a) if the second tab's 401 arrives after the first tab stored the rotated token, it refreshes again (no revoke); the first tab then recovers one CSRF_INVALID. (b) Cross-renderer localStorage lag (finding-57) can cause the same harmless second refresh. (c) A tab on an older bundle takes no lock until reloaded. (d) review-63 N3 (a tab closing mid-refresh loses the rotation) and N4 (restore reads outside the lock) are pre-existing and unchanged.

(e) An admin whose roles were removed gets 403 on the session read, so the tab refreshes instead of skipping. (f) The admin principal on adopt comes from the session read; the client principal from the CSRF read (the profile read cannot give accountStatus). (g) Plan section 8 and finding status are the coordinator's (rule-50); no plan or doc edited, no current document describes the refresh queue.

P-session-hardening (review-51 F4, review-56 note): built, 3 commits on track/p-session-hardening, not pushed or landed. Track rebased onto main 623b377 (p-csrf-stable) on the coordinator's word before any commit.

783384f fix(auth): lower-case the native rotationId before the grace compare. nativeRefresh (shared by native and admin_native) lower-cases input.rotationId once and uses it for derivation, rotateRefresh storage and the grace compare, mirroring webRefresh in 623b377. Before: last_rotation_id is a uuid column (stores lower case), so an upper-case retry inside the 30 s grace failed the compare and revoked the family.

526ee9a fix(session): serialise web cookie refreshes across tabs with Web Locks. createRecoveryQueue moved from api/session/refresh.ts to new api/session/recoveryQueue.ts and takes the scope. With navigator.locks: the cookie refresh and the CSRF_INVALID recovery run under one exclusive lock per scope (boe.admin.session-recovery / boe.client.session-recovery), FIFO across and within tabs. Without it: the old in-tab promise queue, unchanged. sessionEnd.ts exports readStored.

ff0b682 fix(session): confirm a fresh session before skipping a refresh. Corrects 526ee9a, whose skip test (server CSRF token changed during the wait and equals the stored one) could pass with the access cookie still expired (CSRF repair of a pre-DEC-70 session, lost refresh reply, restore elsewhere) and leave a 401 without session end, which AsyncBoundary renders as nothing (rule 4).

Final flow in executeCookieRefresh (admin and client): held user? -> getWebCsrf + holdsUser (finding-50/57 check, unchanged, every path) -> if the stored CSRF token (localStorage boe.<scope>.csrfToken) changed since the tab queued, adoptAnotherTabsRotation reads the session with the access cookie alone (admin GET /v1/admin/session, client GET /v1/client/profile; existing read-only routes, unauthenticated: true so no recursion): refused (non-temporary) -> refresh as before; names another user -> 'replaced' (session ends revoked, no resend); same user -> adopt the CSRF token, return 'rotated' (transport resends once). Temporary failure is rethrown (session and holds kept).

Locks are released when the step settles (resolve or reject); each step is bounded by the transport timeout (20 s per request, GET retries 300/900 ms). No nested lock requests: steps use bareClient, whose refresh coordinator is a stub. Native bearer paths never use the queue.

Compatibility (rule 11): no route, contract, cookie, header, error code, token format or migration change. Released apps v0.14.7..v0.18.0 mint rotationId with crypto.randomUUID (lower case by spec, no polyfill; checked with git grep on each tag), so native tokens are byte-identical for them. Previous backend (CSRF read replaces the token): the lock alone prevents the revoke; the probe makes the second tab adopt, so one refresh there too (test case 2). Web Locks needs a secure context; on plain http or old WebViews the fallback is today's behaviour.

Tests: backend test/integration/authNative.integration.test.ts new case 'an upper-case rotationId replays within the grace and does not revoke the family' (replay returns the same successor, session active with null revocation_reason, successor still rotates).

Frontend new src/shells/crossTabRefresh.test.ts, 10 cases (admin web, client web x 5), two runtime instances sharing jsdom localStorage, a fake navigator.locks (FIFO per name) and a stateful fake server (shared cookie session: CSRF token, access freshness, revoke on stale CSRF): (1) both tabs read at once -> exactly one refresh, no revoke, both signed in with the server's token; (2) same against a CSRF read that replaces the token -> one refresh, no revoke; (3) the waiting tab's session read names another user -> that tab ends revoked, no resend; (4) stored token changed but access cookie not renewed -> probe 401 then a normal refresh; (5) no navigator.locks -> single tab sends exactly read, csrf, refresh, read as before.

Red controls (TESTED, runner, each mutation restored and cmp-identical, tree clean after): RC-A lock bypassed 92ab53bc (8/10 failed); RC-B stored-token check disabled 6e893f4f (8/10); RC-C probe user check removed 1574271b (2/10, case 3); RC-D navigator.locks unguarded f43bc1e3 (2/10, case 5); RC-F refused probe treated as fresh 2f35e821 (2/10, case 4); RC-E native rotationId not lower-cased 3ed2e7a9 (1/8, the new integration case: 401 instead of 200).

Runtime steps for the coordinator (UNVERIFIED; local stack, https or localhost so Web Locks exists):

R1 admin web: sign in, open a second tab on the console, let both finish loading. In DevTools > Application > Cookies delete the access cookie (boe_access, or __Host-boe_access on https). Trigger a read in both tabs at the same moment (click a list or refresh data in each within a second).

R1 expected (Network): one tab shows GET /v1/auth/web/csrf, POST /v1/auth/web/refresh 200, then its read; the other shows GET /v1/auth/web/csrf, GET /v1/admin/session 200, then its read, and no refresh. Both stay signed in; a write in each afterwards succeeds (the first tab may show one 403 CSRF_INVALID then csrf then the same write, only against the previous backend). auth_sessions for the session: state active, revocation_reason null, generation +1.

R2 client web: the same with two investor tabs and cookie boe_client_access; expect GET /v1/auth/client/web/csrf, one POST /v1/auth/client/web/refresh, and in the other tab GET /v1/client/profile instead of a refresh.
R3 single tab (admin and client): delete the access cookie, trigger a read: GET csrf, POST refresh, the read again; no session or profile probe. Unchanged from today.

Doubtful or left: (a) If the second tab's 401 arrives after the first tab already stored the rotated token, its snapshot already holds it, so it refreshes a second time: no revoke (current refresh cookie and current CSRF), the first tab then recovers one CSRF_INVALID once. (b) localStorage reaches other renderers asynchronously (finding-57); a stale read means a second, harmless refresh. (c) A tab still running an older bundle has no lock and can race until reloaded.

(d) The probe adds one GET only when the stored token changed during the wait. (e) The admin probe needs the session read to succeed: an admin whose roles were removed gets 403 there, so the tab refreshes instead (today's path). (f) The admin_native path shares nativeRefresh; only the investor native route has the new integration case. (g) Plan section 8 and finding status are the coordinator's to update (rule-50); no plan or doc edited: no current document describes the refresh queue.
